subject.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups

question: Should canonical Firecrawl and Brave plugin configuration reject prototype-inherited entries and credential fields, matching the own-property rule proposed for legacy and runtime config?
rationale: The PR presents inherited configuration as a security boundary, but completing that boundary intentionally changes programmatic config compatibility; repository policy requires explicit owner review rather than leaving canonical and fallback semantics inconsistent.

options.title: Complete the boundary
options.body: Require own-property checks for canonical plugin entries and relevant fields, retain normal JSON/JSON5 behavior, and add canonical regressions before merge.

options.title: Narrow the hardening scope
options.body: Preserve inherited canonical plugin behavior, remove the broad all-config-path security claim, and limit the PR to the explicitly hardened legacy/runtime paths.

recommendation.title: Complete the boundary
recommendation.body: Require own-property checks for canonical plugin entries and relevant fields, retain normal JSON/JSON5 behavior, and add canonical regressions before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history ties the plugin-owned configuration boundary to the extension ownership refactor in commit 112d1d3a7c409d8de1bd68dcd153a2153f0a762f.
